name: Kontsina (Koltsina)
description: Kontsina (also spelled Koltsina or Kolitsina) is the primary Greek fishing card game. Played by two to four players, it is a game of capture where players aim to take cards from a central layout by matching ranks or summing values. It is deeply ingrained in Greek social life, particularly in kafenio (coffee house) culture, and is valued for its balance of luck and tactical calculation.

overview.description: Kontsina (also spelled Koltsina or Kolitsina) is the primary Greek fishing card game. Played by two to four players, it is a game of capture where players aim to take cards from a central layout by matching ranks or summing values. It is deeply ingrained in Greek social life, particularly in kafenio (coffee house) culture, and is valued for its balance of luck and tactical calculation.

history.origins: Dates to the early 20th century in Greece. It is a descendant of the international Casino family of games, localized with specific scoring points for Clubs and the Diamond 10.
timeline: 1920s: Kontsina becomes common in cafes across Athens and the islands.
1960s: Standard gambling variants emerge with specific coin stakes.
Present: A very common family and holiday game in Greece and the Greek diaspora.
history.cultural: In Greece, 'Koltsina' is often the first card game children learn from their grandparents.
history.evolution: The game evolved to have a 'Last Trick' collection rule, which discourages defensive stalling at the end of the round.

setup.players: Best with 2 players or 4 in partnerships.
setup.deck: Standard 52-card deck. Ace = 1. Jacks/Queens/Kings have no numerical sum value (rank-only).
setup.dealing: Each player receives 4 cards. 4 cards are placed face-up in the center field. The rest form a stock pile.

rules.objective: Score the most points by capturing specific 'score cards' and the largest volume of cards.
rules.gameplay:
1. Play a card from hand to capture from the field.
2. **Rank Match**: Match a Jack, Queen, King, or numeral rank to take it (e.g., King takes King).
3. **Sum Match**: Use a numeral card (e.g., a 9) to take multiple cards whose values sum to it (e.g., 9 takes a 4, a 2, and an Ace (1)).
4. **Discard**: If you cannot capture, leave your card on the table.
5. When hands are empty, deal 4 more cards each from stock until the stock is gone.
keyRules: Capture by matching rank (e.g. 7 takes 7, Queen takes Queen) or by sum (numeral card takes cards summing to it; Ace = 1; face cards only match rank).
If you cannot or do not wish to capture, play a card face up to the tableau (laying).
When hands are empty, dealer deals 4 more cards each from the talon; no new cards to the tableau. Non-dealer plays first after each deal.
Round ends when the last hand is played; remaining tableau cards go to the player who last made a capture.

strategy.basic: Prioritize capturing the **Ten of Diamonds** and the **Two of Clubs**. These cards count for points themselves and contribute to both the 'Most Cards' and 'Most Clubs' categories.
strategy.intermediate: The 'Seven' Rule: Hold your middle-rank cards (5s, 6s, 7s). These are the most flexible for capturing combinations of low cards (Aces, 2s, 3s).
strategy.advanced: Last-Round Denial: If you know the stock is empty, try to be the last person to capture ANY card. The person who makes the last capture gets all the remaining cards on the table for free.
tips: Face cards (J, Q, K) are the easiest to track. If you see three Kings on the table, save your King for as long as possible to capture all four in one 'bomb'.
Pay attention to the Clubs! Winning by just one Club can be the deciding factor in a close match.

variations.name: Points to target
variations.description: Record points each round; first to an agreed total (e.g. 21) wins. Tie on same round: higher score wins; exact tie plays another round.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant only changes win condition; no engine constant overrides needed.

variations.name: Three or four players
variations.description: Play anticlockwise; first to play is to dealer's right. Three players: 4 deals per round; four players: 3 deals per round.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Player count and deal count differ; overrides can be added when engine supports them.

variations.name: Four players in partnerships
variations.description: Two against two; partners sit opposite; combine captured cards into a single pile per team.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Partnership play; overrides for team scoring can be added when supported.

scoring.description: 2 points for most cards (tie at 26 each = no points), 1 for most clubs, 1 for capturing the 2 of clubs (good 2), 1 for the 10 of diamonds (good 10). Majority of round points wins the round; overall winner is whoever wins more rounds. Variant: first to an agreed total (e.g. 21) wins.
scoring.winCondition: Win the majority of rounds (most round wins). Variant: first to reach an agreed point total (e.g. 21) wins.
